title: Joanap: the FBI maps a hidden botnet

scenes.narration: [serious] The FBI pretended to be infected computers to map a botnet.
A botnet is an army of hijacked computers. This one, Joanap, was blamed on North Korea.
A worm called Brambul spread it. Infected PCs gave hackers full control.
Joanap had no boss computer. Victims talked to each other.
In 2019, agents got court approval. With Air Force investigators, the FBI ran fake infected computers. Real victims connected.
That showed who was infected. Victims were warned through internet providers and governments.
U.S. prosecutors had already charged a North Korean programmer. To beat the army, the FBI joined it.

facts.claim: On January 30, 2019 the Justice Department announced a court-authorized effort to map and disrupt the Joanap botnet, using search warrants and court orders under Rule 41
Joanap gives root-level remote control of Windows computers, is peer-to-peer with no central server, is spread by the Brambul worm, and has operated since 2009
The FBI and the Air Force Office of Special Investigations ran servers that mimicked infected peers, collecting IP addresses, ports and timestamps to map the botnet
U.S. victims were notified through their ISPs; foreign victims through their governments
U.S. officials attributed Joanap to the North Korean government; North Korean programmer Park Jin Hyok was charged in 2018 in a complaint alleging a conspiracy that used Brambul
